clue.text: Free spirit to a gardener, figuratively speaking?

indicators.note: to free something is to loosen it, so the letters of these words are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells a gardener to let their spirit run free, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges the nine letters of SPIRIT TO A. The definition is witty: this gardener clips hedges into figures, so works 'figuratively'.
explanation.definitionFit: A topiary specialist clips shrubs into ornamental shapes and figures, hence a gardener working in figures.

clue.text: Rhythm and metre poet worked out

indicators.note: something worked out has been reshaped, so the letters given here are reordered

explanation.surface: A poet works out the rhythm and metre of a new verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges M (metre) with POET.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical pace or beat is the speed of a piece, its rhythmic drive.

clue.text: Band of colour seen by food writer

parts.note: pink is a colour
Keith Floyd was a British TV cook and cookery writer

explanation.surface: A band of colour catches the eye of a food writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a stripe, matching 'of colour', but it is the definition: a rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock group behind The Dark Side of the Moon is a famous musical band.

clue.text: Change a torn form for current supplier

parts.note: to change is to alter

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it, so the letters of 'a torn' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone changes a torn form at the electricity supplier's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like the anagram signal but gives the first piece; 'form' rearranges the letters of 'a torn'.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator producing alternating current in a car engine supplies electrical current.

clue.text: Being low, unfinished, poor, unworthy

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are reworked
the word low loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone describes a person's character as low, incomplete, shabby and undeserving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts LOW to LO; 'poor' rearranges BEING with LO.
explanation.definitionFit: Base or dishonourable conduct is unworthy of respect.

clue.text: Consideration, even if at wit's end

parts.note: though means even if

indicators.note: the final letter of 'wit' is taken

explanation.surface: Someone at their wit's end still shows consideration for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wit's end' supplies T, the last letter of WIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation or reflection on a matter is the act of thinking it over.

clue.text: Chuck Berry's first and last pressure group

parts.note: to chuck is to throw, or lob

indicators.note: the first and last letters of Berry are taken

explanation.surface: Chuck Berry's first and last records are hailed by a campaigning group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck Berry' looks like the rock star, but Chuck is a verb, to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A group campaigning to influence legislators is a lobbying organisation.

clue.text: Lane is given old-fashioned look

parts.note: lo is an archaic word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A country lane is given an old-fashioned appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lane' is Lois Lane, Superman's journalist colleague, not a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Superman's reporter colleague at the Daily Planet bears this first name with the surname Lane.

clue.text: Playwright hit on the head has hard heart

indicators.note: the word for hit on the head contains the next piece
the hard letter sits at the heart, the middle, of the other word

parts.note: to bean someone is to hit them on the head
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A playwright who was struck on the head turns out to be hard-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... heart' puts H in the middle of BEAN. Brendan Behan was an Irish playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Brendan Behan, author of The Quare Fellow, was an Irish dramatist.

clue.text: Chants may upset sailor

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sea shanties may upset a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the nine letters of CHANTS MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sails a pleasure boat is a kind of sailor.

clue.text: Painter coming back some time in the morning

indicators.note: coming back means the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: ten am is a time in the morning

explanation.surface: A painter comes back home at some hour of the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns TEN AM round. Édouard Manet was a French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet, who painted Olympia, was a French artist.

clue.text: Very old coil in the transformer?

indicators.note: a transformer changes things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrician spots an ancient coil inside the transformer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformer' looks like electrical equipment beside 'coil', but rearranges COIL IN THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Stone Age was a prehistoric period, so the term describes something ancient.

clue.text: Old trousers get tucked into shoes

indicators.note: one word is placed within the other

parts.note: oxfords are laced leather shoes
to bag something is to get it

explanation.surface: Someone tucks old trousers into their shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the definition: these wide trousers were a 1920s fashion, and the shoes are named after the same university city.
explanation.definitionFit: Very wide-legged trousers fashionable in the 1920s are now old-fashioned dress.

clue.text: Knucklehead and blockhead join together

parts.note: the head, first letter, of knuckle is K
a nit is a fool or blockhead

explanation.surface: A knucklehead and a blockhead join forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knucklehead' looks like an insult like 'blockhead', but supplies just the head of KNUCKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite or bind, as broken bones do when they mend, is to knit.

clue.text: Two chaps starting experimental factory system

parts.note: Justin is a man's name
Tim is a man's name

indicators.note: the starting letter of experimental is taken

explanation.surface: Two men set up an experimental factory system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes E from 'experimental'.
explanation.definitionFit: A manufacturing method delivering parts only as needed is a production system.

clue.text: Personal assistant lying about fuel

indicators.note: one word goes around the other

parts.note: prone means lying flat

explanation.surface: A personal assistant lies about the fuel bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' looks like telling lies, but means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flammable hydrocarbon gas sold in cylinders is used as fuel.

clue.text: Sovereign in Paris is knocked off a horse

indicators.note: the word is is removed from Paris

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A ruler visiting Paris is thrown from a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked off' removes IS from PARIS, leaving PAR. 'Sovereign' is an adjective here, supreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme or pre-eminent in rank, as a sovereign power is.

clue.text: Geller is introduced to most fantastic service industry

indicators.note: one name is put inside the other letters
fantastic means wild, so the letters of most are rearranged

parts.note: Uri Geller is the spoon-bending illusionist

explanation.surface: Uri Geller is introduced to the most fantastic service industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges the letters of 'most', and 'is introduced to' puts the spoon-bender's first name inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The business of serving holidaymakers and travellers is a service sector.

clue.text: Journalists in house taken up as recruits for the navy

indicators.note: one word sits within another
in a down clue taken up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
the press means journalists

explanation.surface: Journalists in a house are taken up as recruits for the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns the house word upwards, and 'in' puts the journalists inside it. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress was to force men into naval service, as press gangs did.

clue.text: Old soldier embarrassed by film

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
a coat is a thin layer, a film

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier is embarrassed by a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but is a coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A British soldier of past centuries wore a scarlet tunic, earning this nickname.

clue.text: Making sense of French revolutionary? That's crazy

parts.note: touch is one of the five senses

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: Someone tries making sense of a French revolutionary, but it is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns DE (French for of) into ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly mad people are said to be a bit touched in the head.

clue.text: Take advantage of present that's taken aboard

parts.note: to put up is to present, as a candidate or proposal
on means aboard

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a present that was brought on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploiting someone's good nature is imposing on them; the phrase means to impose on.

clue.text: Old man's jest sent up dictator

parts.note: papa is a word for father, old man

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means read upwards

parts.note: to cod is to jest or hoax

explanation.surface: An old man's joke sends up a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns COD into DOC. Papa Doc was François Duvalier, Haiti's dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: François Duvalier, the Haitian despot, was known by this nickname.

clue.text: Drink produced from bananas, packed with energy

indicators.note: one word is filled with the other letter

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A drink is made from bananas with an energy boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented honey and water makes an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Clergyman beheaded for serious crime

indicators.note: the clergyman's word loses its first letter

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman was beheaded for a serious crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops the P of PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a grave criminal offence.

clue.text: They hold up American going west — poet's to follow

indicators.note: the poet comes after the first piece
in an across clue going west means read right to left

parts.note: US means American
Stephen Spender was a poet; with the 's he gives spenders

explanation.surface: An American heads west, with a poet set to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns US into SU. Suspenders are what Americans call braces, and what Britons call stocking garters.
explanation.definitionFit: Straps or garters supporting trousers or stockings keep them up.

clue.text: Avenger's horse

definitions.meaning: John ... was the bowler-hatted agent in the British TV series The Avengers; 's means is

explanation.definitionFit: A spirited riding horse is a steed, and the Avengers agent bore that surname.

clue.text: Change in travel centre when going north on railway

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means read upwards
the centre letters of travel are taken

explanation.surface: There is a change in travel arrangements when heading north by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes AV from TRAVEL, and 'going north' turns it into VA.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to alter or change.

clue.text: He's cut and knocked out — but not hurt

indicators.note: knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer is cut and knocked out but not badly hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' rearranges HES CUT AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Unharmed or uninjured, coming through without a scratch.

clue.text: A question of publication

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute, a question

explanation.definitionFit: A disputed point is an issue, and so is one edition of a magazine.

clue.text: Plant poles in river

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone plants poles in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N S inside TAY, Scotland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered herb of the daisy family is a tansy.

clue.text: After a month, possibly, Red Sea ebbed

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the month

parts.note: Dec is short for December

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of Red Sea can be rearranged

explanation.surface: After a month, perhaps, the Red Sea ebbed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of 'Red Sea'; 'After' puts them behind the abbreviated month. The surface's sea is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrunk or diminished, as a tide does when it ebbs.
